newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN IASS, PHILIPPINE FIRM TO OFFER CARGO SERVICE.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN IASS, PHILIPPINE FIRM TO OFFER CARGO SERVICE.

text.p: Japanese airport services firm IASS Co Ltd said on Monday it has set up a joint venture with a state-owned Philippine firm to provide freight services to Japanese companies in the Philippines.
CLA Air Transport Inc, capitalised at $4 million, is 51 percent-owned by Philippine Aerospace Development Corp and 49 percent-owned by IASS, IASS president Soen Chiyokawa said.
The venture, which uses Manila as its hub, won approval from the Philippine government in early August and is expected to begin operations sometime in 1997.
The venture expects to start by operating five flights per week in a loop operation connecting Tokyo, Cebu and Manila, using DC 10-30 aircraft, he said.
For its operation, CLA Air Transport may lease seven or eight aircraft from a U.S. leasing company, Chiyokawa said, but added that buying its own aircraft was also an option.
"Air cargo in Japan is costly and hard to break even. We can drastically cut costs in the Philippines as operations can be up to one-tenth the cost of those in Japan," Chiyokawa said.
"In addition, there is no need for big investment as the Manila airport is already equipped with good infrastructure established by the U.S. military," he said.
Chiyokawa said Japan's largest carrier Japan Airlines Co Ltd would assist in sales and airport services for Japanese corporate customers.
The venture expects to eventually expand its business into North America and Europe, Chiyokawa said.
